correctness.rationale: For every m>=4 the six graph edges supported on a four-set form the boundary of a 5-simplex, since K4 requires three cover vertices but deletion of any edge leaves a two-cover. Each four-color map takes graph-edge vertices to graph-edge vertices while preserving every two-cover via the witness colors, including equal-color edges. A rainbow four-set maps all six edges bijectively with even orientation parity; a nonrainbow four-set maps at most four distinct image vertices and its H4 cycle vanishes. Complex fourth-root Fourier weighting over the four colors annihilates all T≠U and isolates -24·4^(m−4) times coefficient of z_U; hence the C(m,4) cycle classes are rationally independent for all m. Jonsson Theorem 7.1 supplies the exact H4 rank and proves they span. Every vertex relabeling induces an even permutation on each six-edge tetrahedral fiber, so g(z_T)=z_{gT} and the trace counts invariant four-subsets. Rational invariants of this finite Sn action equal H4 of the quotient after barycentric subdivision. No finite check replaces this universal chain/character argument.

value.rationale: The covering-number-two graph complex is a canonical family with a complete known integral Betti-rank theorem and a recent related Čech homotopy conjecture. Its full Sn-action is a mathematically natural structural invariant not determined by Betti numbers. The theorem supplies an all-m explicit geometric basis, an independent coloring/Fourier detection method, a closed character on every conjugacy class, and one-dimensional quotient rational H4. It is not simply a known rank recomputation or arbitrary finite slice; it does not purport to prove the wedge conjecture or integral-basis theorem.
